name: Queen’s University
header:
Queen’s University
Canada · Mathematics and Statistics MSc (Pattern I thesis / Pattern II project); PhD normally after master’s
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• MSc is the verified normal route from a bachelor’s. Pattern I and Pattern II have different usual funding
durations.
• Funding figures are gross packages from specified earlier years; tuition/fees are deducted from personal
resources. External awards need not be additive.
• OGS 2026-27 is not the Fall 2027 competition; new-student reference reuse is useful prior evidence, not a
current-cycle promise.
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s applicants normally enter MSc: four-year mathematics/statistics or related degree, at least B+ on
the awarding institution’s scale. PhD normally requires relevant master’s, research promise and defined
interests. UChicago mathematics is an appropriate degree field, conditional on grades/completion; direct PhD
exception not established. [dept]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select MSc thesis (Pattern I) or project (Pattern II), and request financial support in the application. Supervisor
agreement is not required before applying; PhD applicants should contact faculty. [dept]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact prospective faculty with transcript/research interests, especially PhD. Gregory Smith explicitly recruits
graduate students and prefers prospective PhDs to begin at master’s level; Ivan Dimitrov welcomes MSc/PhD
projects. [dept] [faculty2] [faculty2a] [faculty12] [faculty12a]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Online application; status available after submission. OGS uses a distinct account/dashboard; prior guide
requires every section marked complete and treats submission as final except personal/referee details by staff.
[apply] [ogsdocs]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Math admission dates are standing, not explicitly Fall 2027. OGS evidence is 2026-27 award cycle, not
2027-28; math funding amount from 2025 and central minimum from 2026-27. [dept] [ogs] [map] [fund]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2025 math PhD map quotes CAD 32,500/year from all sources, years 1-4; 2026-27 central minimum is CAD
25,000/year (not an alternative math offer). MSc amount and 2027-28 rate unverified. Tuition/ancillary fees are
paid by student from package; do not read stipend as net after fees. Covered-month breakdown and summer
amount require offer. [map] [fund]
Years of support [Prior cycle]
August 2025 guide: usual Pattern I MSc support six terms/two years; Pattern II three terms/one year; PhD four
years. Doctoral extension conditional on supervisor recommendation/resources and likely completion; master’s
extensions not normal. [guide]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department normally adds support for international versus domestic tuition difference; not a universal full-fee
waiver. International students eligible for department funding; limited OGS visa-student competition has
Canadian study-permit conditions. [dept] [intl]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Full-time PhD years 1-4, good standing, eligibility/residence for offered TA/RA work and applications for eligible
major awards. Declining package employment reduces funding. External awards count toward guaranteed
package rather than automatically adding to it. [fund]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Must request support on initial admission application; no separate math funding application. OGS is separate.
[fund] [dept]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
OGS CAD 5,000/term for two or three terms (CAD 15,000 full year), nonrenewable, limited international
awards; prior entry criteria A− in each of last two years. 2027-28 eligibility/deadline not verified. Research
fellowships, TA/RA and internal awards compose packages; home-country awards may be relevant. [intl] [ogs]
[fund]
Application fee [Standing rule]
CAD 120 nonrefundable, Visa/Mastercard. If unable to use credit card, contact math graduate assistant for
paper-application route; this is not a fee waiver. [apply] [dept]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Official Physics FAQ explicitly says central SGSPA offers no fee waivers. Mathematics-specific sponsorship
exception not established; confirm before payment if seeking one. [waiver]

sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Mike Roth
Algebraic and Diophantine geometry; positivity/Seshadri constants, rational points, moduli of curves and vector
bundles. [faculty1]
Professor; new-student supervision unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · Seshadri constants on P1 × P1 and applications to the symplectic packing problem
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Gregory G. Smith
Algebraic geometry, commutative algebra and computation; Quot/Hilbert schemes, toric geometry and
positivity. [faculty2] [faculty2a]
Professor; explicitly recruiting graduate students, with preference for future PhD students starting at master’s level.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Classifying smooth Quot schemes
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Noriko Yui
Arithmetic of K3 and Calabi-Yau varieties, modularity of Galois representations and mirror symmetry. [faculty4]
[faculty4a]
Professor; CV lists January-March 2027 MPI Bonn visit. New-student supervision unconfirmed.
Research evidence: listed submitted in 2026 CV; publication year unverified · Certain families of K3 surfaces and their
modularity
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Number theory
M. Ram Murty
Analytic/algebraic number theory, primes, elliptic curves, modular and automorphic forms, L-functions and
sieve methods. [faculty6] [faculty6a]
A.V. Douglas Distinguished University Professor and Queen’s Research Chair; new-student supervision unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Wieferich primes in number fields and the conjectures of Ankeny-Artin-Chowla and Mordell
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Brad Rodgers
Analytic number theory and random matrices; zeta zeros, prime-factor statistics and arithmetic sequences.
[faculty8] [faculty8a]

Queen’s University
Canada · Mathematics and Statistics MSc (Pattern I thesis / Pattern II project); PhD normally after master’s
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• MSc is the verified normal route from a bachelor’s. Pattern I and Pattern II have different usual funding
durations.
• Funding figures are gross packages from specified earlier years; tuition/fees are deducted from personal
resources. External awards need not be additive.
• OGS 2026-27 is not the Fall 2027 competition; new-student reference reuse is useful prior evidence, not a
current-cycle promise.
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s applicants normally enter MSc: four-year mathematics/statistics or related degree, at least B+ on
the awarding institution’s scale. PhD normally requires relevant master’s, research promise and defined
interests. UChicago mathematics is an appropriate degree field, conditional on grades/completion; direct PhD
exception not established. [dept]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select MSc thesis (Pattern I) or project (Pattern II), and request financial support in the application. Supervisor
agreement is not required before applying; PhD applicants should contact faculty. [dept]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact prospective faculty with transcript/research interests, especially PhD. Gregory Smith explicitly recruits
graduate students and prefers prospective PhDs to begin at master’s level; Ivan Dimitrov welcomes MSc/PhD
projects. [dept] [faculty2] [faculty2a] [faculty12] [faculty12a]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Online application; status available after submission. OGS uses a distinct account/dashboard; prior guide
requires every section marked complete and treats submission as final except personal/referee details by staff.
[apply] [ogsdocs]
Cycle verification [Standing rule]
Math admission dates are standing, not explicitly Fall 2027. OGS evidence is 2026-27 award cycle, not
2027-28; math funding amount from 2025 and central minimum from 2026-27. [dept] [ogs] [map] [fund]

Academic application [Standing rule]
Standing January 15 deadline; late applications accepted through April 30 while places remain. September is
normal entry. No explicit 2027 year, clock time or time zone found. [dept]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]

24, 2026 is closed and must not be rolled forward. [dept] [ogsdates]

Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2025 math PhD map quotes CAD 32,500/year from all sources, years 1-4; 2026-27 central minimum is CAD

amount require offer. [map] [fund]

August 2025 guide: usual Pattern I MSc support six terms/two years; Pattern II three terms/one year; PhD four
years. Doctoral extension conditional on supervisor recommendation/resources and likely completion; master’s
extensions not normal. [guide]

waiver. International students eligible for department funding; limited OGS visa-student competition has
Canadian study-permit conditions. [dept] [intl]

Pay attention to

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s applicants normally enter MSc: four-year mathematics/statistics or related degree, at least B+ on
the awarding institution’s scale. PhD normally requires relevant master’s, research promise and defined
interests. UChicago mathematics is an appropriate degree field, conditional on grades/completion; direct PhD
exception not established. [dept]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select MSc thesis (Pattern I) or project (Pattern II), and request financial support in the application. Supervisor
agreement is not required before applying; PhD applicants should contact faculty. [dept]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Contact prospective faculty with transcript/research interests, especially PhD. Gregory Smith explicitly recruits
graduate students and prefers prospective PhDs to begin at master’s level; Ivan Dimitrov welcomes MSc/PhD
projects. [dept] [faculty2] [faculty2a] [faculty12] [faculty12a]

Online application; status available after submission. OGS uses a distinct account/dashboard; prior guide
requires every section marked complete and treats submission as final except personal/referee details by staff.

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
2025 math PhD map quotes CAD 32,500/year from all sources, years 1-4; 2026-27 central minimum is CAD
25,000/year (not an alternative math offer). MSc amount and 2027-28 rate unverified. Tuition/ancillary fees are

amount require offer. [map] [fund]

August 2025 guide: usual Pattern I MSc support six terms/two years; Pattern II three terms/one year; PhD four
years. Doctoral extension conditional on supervisor recommendation/resources and likely completion; master’s
extensions not normal. [guide]
